ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The deflection of ions using magnetic fields is a widely applied technique in scientific instruments. As shown in the figure, there are two sufficiently long regions, Region I and Region II, both with a width of $L$ and boundaries parallel to the $x$-axis, located in the first quadrant of the Oxy plane (the plane of the paper). Region I has a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction of magnitude $B_{1}$, and Region II has a magnetic field with a magnetic induction of magnitude $B_{2}$, both directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper. The lower boundary of Region II coincides with the $x$-axis. An ion source located at $(0,3L)$ emits a beam of positive ions with mass $m$, charge $q$, and a velocity direction at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with respect to the $x$-axis, which are directed towards the magnetic field regions along the plane of the paper. Neglecting the gravity of the ions and their interactions, and ignoring the boundary effects of the magnetic fields.

1. Determine the maximum velocity $v_{1}$ of the ions such that they do not enter Region II.
2. Calculate the time $t$ the ions spend moving within the magnetic field.
3. If $B_{2}=2B_{1}$, determine the minimum velocity $v_{2}$ of the ions that can reach the position $y=\frac{L}{2}$.
4. If $B_{2}=\frac{B_{1}}{L}y$, and the number of ions emitted from the ion source is uniformly distributed with respect to speed in the range $\frac{B_{1}q L}{m} \sim \frac{6B_{1}q L}{m}$, determine the ratio $\eta$ of the number of ions entering the fourth quadrant to the total number of ions.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows the Oxy coordinate system, the x-axis is the lower boundary of region II, and the y-axis is marked with O, L, 2L, 3L. Region I is a gray long strip region located from y=L to y=2L, and region II is a striped long strip region located from y=0 to y=L; the boundaries of both regions are parallel to the x-axis. The ion source is drawn near (0,3L), and the velocity arrow points to the lower right, making 60° with the horizontal dashed line. Reasoning: After positive ions enter the magnetic field perpendicular to the paper inward, they undergo circular deflection. Let a=B1 q L/m. When the speed is v, in region I the radius R1=mv/(qB1). The ions enter region I from y=2L, and the incident velocity direction is 60° downward to the right; the center of the circle is in the direction perpendicular to the velocity, and the vertical difference from the incident point to the center is R1/2, so the lowest point of this circular trajectory is lower than the incident height by R1/2. 1. The critical situation of not entering region II is that the lowest point just touches y=L, that is, 2L-R1/2=L, so R1=2L, v1=qB1R1/m=2B1qL/m. 2. In this critical trajectory, after the ion enters region I from y=2L, it returns to y=2L and leaves the magnetic field, and the velocity direction turns through 120°=2π/3. The angular velocity is ω=qB1/m, so the time in the magnetic field is t=(2π/3)/ω=2πm/(3qB1). 3. If B2=2B1, then after entering region II the radius R2=mv/(qB2)=R1/2. Let the radius in region I be R1. When the ion enters region II at y=L, it maintains tangential continuity, and the lowest point of the new circular trajectory decreases as R1 increases; according to circle geometry, the height of the lowest point in region II is 3L/2-R1/4. When it can just reach y=L/2, 3L/2-R1/4=L/2, giving R1=4L, so v2=qB1R1/m=4B1qL/m. 4. If B2=(B1/L)y, first find the horizontal velocity when entering region II. In region I, from dvx=-(q/m)B1 dy, from y=2L to y=L, vx increases by B1qL/m=a; at incidence vx=v/2, so vx(L)=v/2+a. In region II, B=(B1/L)y, and from dvx=-(q/m)B(y)dy, from y=L to y=0, vx increases again by ∫0^L qB1 y/(mL) dy=a/2. Therefore vx(0)=v/2+3a/2. The magnetic field does no work, and the speed is still v; to be able to reach and enter below the x-axis, the vertical velocity at y=0 needs to be real and downward, and the critical condition satisfies v=vx(0), that is, v=(v+3a)/2, giving the threshold v=3a=3B1qL/m. The speed is uniformly distributed on [a,6a], and the proportion that can enter the fourth quadrant is (6a-3a)/(6a-a)=3/5=60%.
